 ‘Hunger Games’ star Mckenna Grace is a girl on fire 
 By Sabine Snyder 
 Published 
 Nov. 17, 2026, 8:00 a.m. ET

 What’s your favorite movie or TV show of the past decade? Whatever your answer, there’s a good chance Mckenna Grace was in it. And if she wasn’t, well, give Hollywood a minute. Maybe she was playing a younger version of your favorite actress, solving supernatural mysteries, or giving Chris Evans a run for his money as the smartest person in the room. Whatever the role, it’s obvious that Grace has a knack for making an impression, even when she’s sharing the screen with some of Hollywood’s most legendary names.
 It’s hard to deny that the actress became something of a Hollywood staple for playing younger versions of established stars. Young Margot Robbie in I, Tonya ? That’s Grace. Young Brie Larson in Captain Marvel ? Also Grace. And perhaps her most convincing younger-self casting yet: Kiernan Shipka’s Sabrina Spellman in Chilling Adventures of Sabrina .
 But the actress has come a long way from her days as Hollywood’s go-to younger self. With roles in everything from The Handmaid’s Tale to Ghostbusters: Afterlife , Grace has steadily built a filmography of her own, and now, she’s headed to the arena.
 Grace stars as Maysilee Donner and her twin sister, Marilee Donner, in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , the latest installment in the blockbuster franchise. With the highly anticipated prequel bringing her into one of the most recognizable fictional worlds, there’s no better time to look back at how Grace went from playing Hollywood’s younger leading ladies to becoming a leading lady in her own right.
 Wilson Webb 
 Who Is Mckenna Grace? From Texas Kid to Hollywood Regular 
 Born in Grapevine, Texas, Grace began acting at just five years old . Her first major screen appearances included guest roles in television shows like Crash & Bernstein and The Goodwin Games before she started landing more prominent parts.
 One of her earliest breakout roles came in Gifted , where she starred opposite Chris Evans as Mary Adler, a mathematically gifted young girl caught in a custody battle between her uncle and grandmother. The film gave Grace an opportunity to hold her own alongside none other than Captain America himself, and she certainly didn’t waste it.
 Around the same time, Grace was becoming a familiar face in another very specific corner of Hollywood: playing the younger versions of some of its biggest stars.
 Hollywood’s Go-To Younger Self 
 There was a point when it seemed like every major white actress needed a younger counterpart on screen, and Grace was more than happy to oblige.
 Beyond her high-profile film roles, Grace also took on younger versions of familiar TV characters, including Emma Swan ( Jennifer Morrison ) in Once Upon a Time , Caroline Forbes ( Candice King ) in The Vampire Diaries and Theo Crain ( Kate Siegel ) in The Haunting of Hill House . 
 Of course, she wasn’t exclusively playing other people’s younger selves. Grace showed off her ability to lead a project in The Bad Seed , portraying a seemingly sweet young girl with a much darker side. She also took on the role of Judy Warren in Annabelle Comes Home , adding another horror credit to her growing resume.
 Photos: Everett Collection 
 From ‘Ghostbuster’ to ‘The Handmaid’s Tale’ 
 As Grace got older, her roles began to expand beyond the younger versions that initially made her so recognizable.
 She joined the Ghostbusters universe as Phoebe Spengler in Ghostbusters: Afterlife , reprising the role in Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire . Grace also delivered a memorable performance as Jan Broberg in Peacock’s true-crime drama A Friend of the Family and as Esther Keyes in The Handmaid’s Tale . In 2025 she joined the ensemble cast of Anniversary , starring alongside Diane Lane , Kyle Chandler , Zoey Deutch and Dylan O’Brien .
 More recently, Grace portrayed Clara Grant, the daughter of Morgan Grant ( Allison Williams ), in the Colleen Hoover adaptation Regretting You . But let’s be honest: The real love story to come out of that movie was Grace and her co-star Mason Thames . After a press tour that sparked romance rumors, the two confirmed their relationship by making their red carpet debut together at the Oscars in March. We’ll take that movie magic!
 And because apparently there aren’t enough hours in the day for this actress, Grace has also made her mark in voice acting, lending her voice to Skye in the PAW Patrol movies and playing young Daphne in Scoob! .
 Murray Close/Lionsgate 
 Mckenna Grace Is Headed to Panem 
 Regretting You may have given Grace one of the cutest real-life rom-com romances yet, but it also delivered the news of a lifetime: She was joining The Hunger Games . Grace told ScreenRant that she received the call confirming she’d landed the role of Maysilee Donner while filming the movie, where several of her co-stars happened to be reading Suzanne Collins’ book . Naturally, they were quick to connect the dots when Grace hinted that she’d received some exciting news, nearly blowing her secret before the official casting announcement even dropped.
 And for Grace, this wasn’t just another franchise role. In a Cosmopolitan interview , she said she’s been a self-proclaimed Hunger Games superfan for years, making fan edits, dreaming up headcanons and even keeping a giant poster of the series on her wall. She also recalled telling director Francis Lawrence that she’d read the books and watched the movies countless times — and that getting to run toward the cornucopia herself felt surreal.
 In The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , Grace stars as Maysilee Donner, a District 12 tribute who enters the Second Quarter Quell alongside a young Haymitch Abernathy ( Joseph Zada ). She’ll also play Maysilee’s twin sister, Merrilee. The prequel takes audiences back to the 50th Hunger Games, decades before Katniss Everdeen ( Jennifer Lawrence ) ever volunteered as tribute, offering fans another glimpse into the brutal world of Panem.
 Grace has even kept a journal for Maysilee, filled with details she knows fans will appreciate, and made a point of advocating for the character’s signature braid and pin — a look previously brought to life only in a popular 2011 fan-made short film that gave Maysilee her first on-screen portrayal. That enthusiasm is exactly what makes her casting so exciting. She’s approaching this role not just as an actress, but as a fellow fangirl who has spent years loving and growing up with this world. Now, she gets to help bring another chapter of Panem’s story to the big screen.
 If her track record is any indication, Grace will have no trouble bringing her own flair to Maysilee while staying true to the qualities that make the character — and the franchise — so beloved. 
 What can she say? She’s just doing acting. 
 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping comes out Nov. 20, 2026 in theaters everywhere.
